skill_name: KPI Metric Definition & Business Impact Analysis
subtopic: Correlation Analysis (Pearson vs Spearman Rank Correlation)
question_text: [KPI Metric Definition & Business Impact Analysis - Q40] Why is Spearman's rank correlation preferred over Pearson's correlation when assessing the relationship between two variables exhibiting a non-linear but strictly monotonic relationship with extreme outliers?

options.text: Spearman evaluates monotonic association based on ranks rather than linear raw values, making it robust to non-linearity and outliers
Pearson correlation only works on categorical text
Pearson requires zero degrees of freedom

answer_explanation: Pearson measures strict linear proportionality and is sensitive to extreme values. Spearman assesses whether values increase together monotonically by ranking observations.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: Pearson measures strict linear proportionality and is sensitive to extreme values. Spearman assesses whether values increase together monotonically by ranking observations.
